title: prefill-decode-pipeline: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap + kernel scheduler optimizations
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Performance: Reduce p50 latency by ~12% for long-context models; throughput +15% for high-concurrency workloads. No API changes. Rollout via canary with automatic rollback on regression.
description: Motivation: Prefill and decode stages have historically been executed in discrete phases which leaves GPU cycles underutilized for long-context workloads and increases end-to-end latency. This PR implements three complementary optimizations: 1) chunked prefill which splits large prefill sequences into smaller chunks to enable overlap with decode; 2) speculative prefill where we speculatively compute KV cache for likely next-token prefixes to reduce stalls on decode; and 3) a stage-overlap scheduler that more aggressively pipelines prefill and decode on the same device while honoring KV cache consistency. Implementation touches runtime/kernel selection, KV cache lifecycle, and the continuous-batching path. Key design points: chunked prefill is opt-in per-model via config and defaults to conservative chunk sizes; speculative prefill uses probabilistic thresholds derived from token frequency histograms and can be disabled per-route; the kernel scheduler selects smaller, latency-optimized kernels for short decode steps and throughput-optimized kernels for prefill chunks. Tests & validation: unit tests for KV cache invariants and scheduler policies, an expanded perf harness with synthetic and real workloads, and canary runs on the 4-GPU pool. Performance: p50 latency for 8k-context benchmark reduced from 210ms to 185ms (~11.9%); end-to-end throughput on the 4-GPU pool increased ~15% for batch size 8; KV cache hit-rate improved by ~3.4% in mixed workloads. Rollout plan: staged canary (5%)->10%->50%->100% with automated perf checks and rollback on >3% regression in p50 or increased error rate. Checklist: [x] design doc linked in Linear ENG-2789; [x] unit and integration tests added; [x] perf benchmarks and CI perf-suite passing in canary; [x] documented config flags and release notes. Related: PRs that iterated on prefill/decode overlap in the repo (see history of prefill optimizations).
